notes.text: The most important part of the process is the abrasive action created by vigorously rubbing your hands together to loosen transient microorganisms.

citations.quote: It is the abrasive action obtained by vigorously rubbing the surfaces being cleaned that loosens the transient microorganisms on the hands.

notes.text: While scrubbing, you must pay particular attention to removing any soil from underneath your fingernails.

notes.text: The vigorous rubbing phase must last at least 10 to 15 seconds, but the total cleaning procedure from start to finish must take at least 20 seconds.

Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds

notes.text: Never wash your hands in a food preparation sink, as this practice can lead to avoidable contamination of the sink and food products.

citations.quote: It is inappropriate to wash hands in a food preparation sink since this may result in avoidable contamination of the sink and the food prepared therein.

notes.text: The instructions suggest using a cloth towel at home, but regulations require specific hand-drying methods such as individual disposable towels or a continuous towel system.

citations.quote: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device

notes.text: To prevent recontamination after rinsing, you should also use a paper towel to operate the sink faucet handles.

notes.text: Ensuring hands are completely dry is vital as moisture increases the risk of transferring bacteria and viruses to other surfaces.

notes.text: Hand sanitizer cannot be used as a substitute for washing with soap; regulations require that each handwashing sink be provided with a supply of hand cleaning soap for employee use.

citations.quote: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

notes.text: The hand antiseptic used must be an FDA-approved drug or contain active antimicrobial ingredients listed in the FDA monograph to ensure safety and effectiveness.

notes.text: Regulatory standards use the term "hand antiseptic" instead of "hand sanitizer" because skin agents typically achieve a much lower microbial reduction than the 5-log standard required for equipment.

citations.quote: The Food Code definition of "sanitizer" requires a minimum microbial reduction of 5 logs, which is equal to a 99.999% reduction.
